reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease
clinicalPearls: The acronym summarises the core features: mental retardation, enteropathy, deafness, peripheral neuropathy, ichthyosis, and keratodermia
An autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic variants in AP1S1, encoding a subunit of the adaptor protein complex 1 (AP-1) that governs intracellular vesicular trafficking

Copper indices resemble those of Wilson disease and Menkes disease combined: low serum copper and caeruloplasmin alongside high hepatic copper, reflecting mislocalisation of the copper ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B
Congenital or infantile diarrhoea (enteropathy) may be severe and life-threatening in early life
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss and a length-dependent sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy develop over time
Skin findings include congenital ichthyosis and palmoplantar keratoderma reflecting disturbed epidermal trafficking
Cholestatic liver disease with copper accumulation can occur, and copper-modulating therapy has been explored
Diagnosis rests on the characteristic multisystem pattern confirmed by AP1S1 sequencing
reference.pathophysiology: MEDNIK syndrome results from loss-of-function variants in AP1S1, which encodes the sigma-1A subunit of the heterotetrameric adaptor protein complex 1. AP-1 mediates clathrin-dependent sorting of transmembrane cargo between the trans-Golgi network and endosomes. Disrupted AP-1 function impairs the correct trafficking and localisation of the copper-transporting ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B, producing a mixed copper-handling defect that biochemically overlaps both Menkes and Wilson disease. The same trafficking failure perturbs epidermal keratinocyte differentiation, enterocyte function, myelination, and neuronal development, generating the combined dermatological, gastrointestinal, auditory, neurological, and cognitive phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Menkes disease and occipital horn syndrome (ATP7A defects)
Peripheral neuropathies with deafness (e.g. some Charcot-Marie-Tooth variants)
Other congenital disorders of glycosylation and trafficking
additionalInvestigations: Hepatic copper quantification and liver function tests
Nerve conduction studies for peripheral neuropathy
Skin examination and, where needed, biopsy for ichthyosis and keratoderma
redFlags: Severe infantile enteropathy with dehydration and failure to thrive
Progressive cholestatic liver disease with copper overload
Rapidly progressive hearing loss or neuropathy
Sepsis complicating protracted diarrhoea in infancy
reference.prognosis: A chronic multisystem disorder; early enteropathy can be life-threatening, while survivors face progressive hearing loss, neuropathy, and variable cognitive impairment, with liver involvement contributing to long-term morbidity.
pitfalls: Interpreting the copper indices as isolated Wilson or Menkes disease and missing the trafficking diagnosis
Attributing infantile diarrhoea solely to infection or allergy
Overlooking the syndromic significance of combined skin, hearing, and nerve findings
Assuming copper chelation alone addresses the underlying multisystem defect
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Zinc acetate, with copper-modulating therapy as used in Wilson disease, to correct the disturbed copper handling and limit hepatic copper accumulation
Nutritional support for the enteropathy, including parenteral nutrition during severe infantile diarrhoea
Emollients, keratolytics and topical or systemic retinoids for ichthyosis and palmoplantar keratoderma
Hearing aids or cochlear implantation for progressive sensorineural hearing loss, with physiotherapy and supportive care for the peripheral neuropathy
Developmental, educational and communication support for cognitive impairment
Monitor liver function and hepatic copper, with periodic audiometry and nerve conduction studies
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and test at-risk family members
Coordinate care through a metabolic, dermatology, neurology and audiology multidisciplinary team
